title: Geometry and first-direct-image vanishing of a regular point blowup
statement: Let $X$ be an integral regular Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], with Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Let $p\in X$ be a closed point such that $\dim\mathcal O_{X,p}=2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $b:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_pX\to X$ be the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] of the reduced closed point. Then $X'$ is integral, regular and Noetherian. The morphism $b$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and is an isomorphism over $X\setminus\{p\}$. For every closed point $q\in X'$ with $b(q)=p$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{X',q}$ has dimension $2$. Finally $R^1b_*\mathcal O_{X'}=0$, where $R^1b_*$ means the first right derived functor of direct image of module sheaves, equivalently degree-one cohomology of the derived direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], on the Zariski topology.
